**A-41 Part 7's *"no per-screen-size rule"* is not violated and is hereby clarified in place:** it forbids a
**frame** that depends on a measurement — no `viewBox`, pane count or pane membership may vary with screen
size, and none does. A CSS box that resolves at layout measures nothing, keeps W1 intact, and leaves the
frame byte-identical in bare Node.

> **Completed by A-50, revision 34 (QA R37-4).** The `max-height` clamp fixes the **wide** direction only:
> **50 of 239** single-country libraries have a pane too *tall* for it and still letterbox (`MV` at 22.0%,
> `CL` measured at 33.4%), and the same clamp letterboxes the shipped sample horizontally on a desktop
> (**76.8%** at 1440 × 700). A-50 makes the box the map in both directions with one declaration, and
> replaces this Part's *"fills its box"* criterion with a symmetric one. `aspect` itself does not move.

**Part 7 — Part 5's invariants, amended and extended.**

- **I2 (restated).** Every `country.paneId` names a pane in `panes`; every `pane.codes` is exactly the set of
  countries carrying that `paneId`, **and `pane.codes` is in canonical row order**. The `countries` array's
  own order is C9's paint order and is no longer canonical.
- **I8 (new) — the key point is a point of the country.** Every key point lies within the bounding box of
  that code's principal ring. Measured over all 239 codes: 176 fall inside their own rings and the maximum
  distance from a key point to its own geometry is **203 km** (`NO`), against **16,598 km** (`KI`) under C2.
- **I9 (new) — order-independence.** For any input, permuting `points` permutes `clusterPoints`' answer and
  changes nothing else: the induced partition of the points is identical under every ordering.
- **I10 (new) — nothing is painted out of reach.** No country's fill is entirely contained in the fill of a
  country emitted after it in `frame.countries`.
- **I1, I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 are unchanged**, and round 36 verified all seven hold; this ruling may not cost
  any of them. I6 (byte-identical determinism) is strengthened rather than threatened: C3′ removes the last
  input to the frame that was not the data.
  > **I1, I3 and I5 are restated by A-49 Part 8, revision 34** (a code with a detached part is drawn in two
  > panes, `panes.length` becomes 1…4, and a `'detached'` pane is always last), and **I11–I15 are added**.
  > **I8, I9 and I10 are untouched** — A-49 changes no key point (I12 proves the identity bit-for-bit over
  > all 239 codes at five thresholds), no partition and no paint order.

**Part 8 — the five MINORs, routed.**

| Finding | Route | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **R36-3** — C4's *"≥1.5× margin"* is not a property of the index | **fixed here**, Part 4 | it is a false sentence in my own ruling; the constant does not move, so there is nothing for a builder to do |
| **R36-4** — `weight` is trips × countries | **fixed here** as a disclosure, residue 4 below; **no code change** | the metric is right and the alternative is measurably worse — see below |
| **R36-5** — the main pane fills 42.6% of its box at 390 px | **fixed here** (Part 6, one frame field), **built by the builder in I-8g** | the CSS-only version needs arithmetic in the view, which A-40 Part 2 forbids — it needed a line from me before it could be a one-line fix |
| **R36-6** — dark-mode country ink vs sea is 2.87:1 | **builder, I-8g** | a token value with a measured floor and no design content; I-8a's pairing, first measured here |
| **R36-7** — 2 of 239 have no self-hit-testable fill | **half fixed here** (C9), **half deferred**, residue 6 | the containment half is provable and free; the shared-pixel half is not an ordering problem at all |

**R36-4, answered rather than deflected.** `weight(cluster) = Σ tripIds.length` counts **country-visits**, so
it rises with both the number of trips and the number of countries: one six-country European trip (6) outranks
five separate Japan trips (5). The obvious alternative — count **distinct trips** — is refused on two measured
grounds. **(a) It is not additive**, and C5's whole test is the majority comparison `2 × weight(primary) > W`;
a trip touching two clusters would be counted in both, `Σ weight(cluster) > W`, and the comparison would stop
meaning anything. **(b) It regresses R33-1 on the only real library we have**: the shipped sample is **one
trip** (`trip-europe-2026`, verified — all seven codes carry that single id), so distinct-trip weights are
1 and 1, C5 correctly refuses to split a tie, and the map goes straight back to the 194.5° frame this whole
arc exists to remove. So the metric stands and residue 4 stops under-disclosing it.

**Part 9 — residues, stated rather than solved.**

1′ *(supersedes A-41 Part 8 residue 1′, which is withdrawn)*. **A country whose own box crosses ±180° no
   longer has a meaningless key point** — C2′ puts `KI` on Kiritimati, `FJ` on Viti Levu, `UM` on its largest
   island and `RU` in Siberia, all within 900 km of their own ground. What survives is narrower and is about
   the **extent, not the key**: a pane containing such a code is still globe-wide, because `mapBounds` takes
   min/max over that country's box. Fixing *that* is dateline-aware bounds in core, which A-41 Part 1 refuses
   on measurement and this ruling does not reopen.
2. **A pane still has no name** (A-41 residue 2, unchanged).
3. **The third pane can still be wide** (A-41 residue 3, unchanged).
4. *(supersedes A-41 Part 8 residue 4)*. **`weight` counts country-visits, not trips and not days.** It rises
   with the number of trips **and** with the number of countries in the cluster, so one six-country trip
   outranks five single-country trips; and a weekend and a month count the same, because the row carries no
   per-country day attribution (A-31 Part 5 residue 2, §8.5's `Visit` unbuilt). Part 8 above records why the
   alternative is worse. Since the same quantity is C6's first ranking key and country count is its second,
   country count is felt twice; that is disclosed, not hidden, and it decides only which pane is larger.
5. **Single linkage chains** (new, from C3′). A component may be joined through intermediate countries, so
   `US CA GL IS GB` is one wide pane. This is honest — the traveller really did visit the countries in
   between — and C5 still decides whether anything splits. With all 239 codes in a library the world is **one**
   component and the frame is one honest world map, which is the right answer for someone who has been
   everywhere. **Reopen if a real library produces a main pane wider than ~120° through a chain**; the bounded
   remedy would be a diameter cap on a component, and it is deliberately not built now.
6. **Two countries can share a screen pixel** (new, from R36-7's other half). `MF` and `SX` are two halves of
   one 90 km² island; at any frame that also fits the rest of a library they occupy the same pixel, and
   whichever paints last owns it. **No paint order fixes that** — it is a scale property, not a topology one —
   and the honest remedy is the code-chip list under the map, which names and reaches every country
   unconditionally. A-41 constraint 3's *"visibly represented and attributable"* is met there. Reopen only if
   the surface ever loses the chip list.

#### A-49 — the extent is decided by the same rule the clustering is: a country's geometry is its *parts*, a pane frames the parts its subject is connected to, and the parts it is not connected to get a pane of their own (revision 34, QA **R37-1**, **R37-3**; ROADMAP **I-8h**)

*(This ruling **amends A-41 and A-48 in place** and is read **with** both, never instead of them. Unchanged
and still binding: A-41 Part 1's diagnosis, Part 2's four constraints, **C1**, **C4′**, **C5**, **C6**,
Part 4's padding term, Part 6's one-kernel requirement, W1/W2/W3, and the whole of Part 7's do-not-build
list except the pane cap. A-48's **C2′**, **C3′**, **C4′** and **C9** are unchanged in every output they
produce — C2′'s key point is preserved **bit-for-bit** by construction, and the proof is Part 2 below.
**A-42 is untouched in full.** What moves: **C8** (the extent), **C7**'s cap, Part 5's frame shape and
**I1**/**I2**/**I3**/**I5**, and A-48 C9's consequence 2, which is factually wrong and is corrected here.
Round 37 confirmed that every clause of A-48 is implemented exactly as written; as at round 36, **the
defect is in what the ruling specifies, not in what was built**.)*

**Part 1 — the defect, in one sentence, and the numbers.**

A-48 gave the map **two different answers to "where is this country"** and used one of them to decide
clustering and the other to decide the viewport. C2′ decides *which countries share a pane* from the
country's **principal ring**; **C8 was not touched by A-48** and still fits `mapBounds` over the four
corners of **every index entry `box`** of every code in the pane — for `FR` that box reaches French Guiana
at −54.5°E. So the pane knows France is in France and then frames the Atlantic anyway.

Re-derived by me over the shipped index before ruling, and it is worse than *"the caption is fixed"*:

| the ship-gate library (`FR` ×2, `GR` ×1) | A-48 as shipped | this ruling |
|---|---|---|
| main pane extent | **81.13° × 49.10°** (`viewBox` 84.37 × 52.34) | **31.20° × 16.23°** (`viewBox` 32.44 × 17.48) |
| land, by even-odd sampling of the pane | **1.95%** | **14.02%** |
| Greece's own box as a share of the pane | **1.009%** | **7.86%** — **7.8× the area, 2.79× linear** |
| Greece at 390 px | 27 × 29 px = **783 px²** | ≈ 71 × 76 px ≈ **5,370 px²** |
| French Guiana | a speck in the corner of the main pane | its own pane, **2.87° × 3.70°**, **59.8% land** |

Round 37's other framing of the same defect is that Greece was **27,079 px²** under I-8d, in an inset of its
own. That number is not a target and this ruling does not chase it: I-8d put Greece in an inset **because
it had mis-clustered France into the Atlantic** (R36-1), and captioned Greece *"shown separately"* from a
country 1,900 km away. France and Greece are one cluster; the honest answer is one pane, and the defect was
never the pane count — it was the rectangle. This ruling makes that rectangle 7.9× smaller in area.

**Part 2 — the rule. One concept, and it is the one A-48 already introduced.**

A-48's insight was that *a country's position is a property of its principal landmass, not of its bounding
rectangle*. The generalisation is that **a country's geometry is a set of landmasses**, and that both
questions — which countries share a pane, and what rectangle that pane looks through — are answered by
single linkage at the same threshold over the same kind of point. Nothing here reads which country a code
is; nothing here detects an overseas territory; there is no list, no carve-out and no second constant.

> **P (new, in core) — the parts of a country.**
> `countryParts(code, index, thresholdKm): CountryPart[]`. Take **every ring of every index entry carrying
> that code** with at least three points (§8.4 A-27 allows two entries; they are one country). Give each
> ring the centre of its own bounding box as its point, and take the **connected components** of those
> points under `clusterPoints(points, thresholdKm)` — A-41 Part 6's one kernel, A-48 C3′'s semantics, no
> second implementation. Each component is a **part**:
>
> ```ts
> export type CountryPart = {
>   /** `[minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat]` over this part's rings. Derived, never hand-written. */
>   box: CountryBox;
>   /** The box centre of this part's greatest-absolute-spherical-area ring; ties by index order. */
>   key: LatLng;
>   /** This part's rings, in index order (entry order, then ring order). */
>   rings: readonly CountryRing[];
>   /** The part holding the code's greatest-area ring. Exactly one part per code carries it. */
>   principal: boolean;
> };
> ```
>
> Parts are returned in ascending order of their lowest ring position in the index. A code the index does
> not carry, or that carries no ring of three points, has **no parts**: `countryParts` returns `[]`, and the
> frame treats `[]` exactly as `countryKeyPoint`'s `null` — the code goes to `missing`, stated rather than
> dropped (A-40 clause 3).

> **C8′ (supersedes C8) — a pane frames what its subject is connected to.**
> For each pane produced by C5/C6/C7, let `P` be **every part of every code in that pane**. Take the
> connected components of `P`'s key points under `clusterPoints(·, WORLD_CLUSTER_THRESHOLD_KM)`. The pane's
> **in-frame set** is the union of the components containing at least one member code's **principal** part;
> every other part of `P` is **detached**.
> `pane.bounds` is `core.mapBounds` over the four corners of each **in-frame** part's `box` — still three
> calls to core where there was one, and **the client still computes no bounds**.

> **C8″ — nothing is cropped: the detached pane.**
> The detached parts of **every** pane, taken together, form one further pane appended after the geographic
> ones: `id: 'detached'`, `role: 'detached'`, `bounds` = `mapBounds` over their boxes, `viewBox` padded by
> Part 4's identical term, `codes` = the codes contributing to it in canonical row order. It exists **iff**
> at least one part is detached. It is not ranked, does not participate in C5's `W` or C6's ordering, and
> is never `panes[0]`.

> **C7′ (supersedes C7's cap sentence only).** At most **three geographic panes** — primary, second-ranked,
> and the union of every remaining cluster, exactly as C7 says — **plus the detached pane when it exists**.
> So `panes.length` is 1…4. Everything else in C7 is unchanged, including *"every drawn country is in at
> least one pane, always"*.

**Why the in-frame set is exactly one component, which is what makes this cheap and provable.** A pane's
member codes are a connected component of the **country** graph, whose vertices are C2′ key points and whose
edges join pairs under the threshold. Every C2′ key point *is* a principal part's key (Part 3 below proves
the identity), and `P` contains every principal part of every member, so the part graph over `P` contains
every edge the country graph had. The members' principal parts are therefore all in one part-component. The
in-frame set is that component; no tie-break, no scan order, no arbitrary choice enters anywhere.

**Part 3 — what does *not* change, and why that is the point.**

- **`countryKeyPoint` is not touched, and C2′'s output is preserved bit-for-bit.** The greatest-area ring of
  a country is the greatest-area ring of its own part, so `countryParts(code, index, t).find(p => p.principal).key`
  **is** `countryKeyPoint(code, index)`, for every threshold. Verified by me over all 239 codes at
  `t ∈ {1, 100, 1000, 4000, 20000}` km: **0 mismatches, `Object.is`-exact on both fields**. That identity is
  an invariant below (I12), and it is why **I8, C3′, C4′'s ten pinned pairs, C5, C6 and every pane's
  *membership* are untouched by this ruling**. This ruling changes rectangles, not partitions.
- **The kernel is not touched.** `clusterPoints` is called twice more with different points; its semantics,
  its signature and its callers `clusterStops`/`focusCluster` are unchanged, so **I9 holds unchanged, the
  day map is byte-identical at 90 km by construction, and `npm run golden && npm run sample` cannot move**.
  A-41 Part 6's stop-and-report rule still applies and is expected never to fire.
- **R33-1's reference frame survives, and its main pane is byte-identical.** For
  `["AT","CZ","DE","GB","HR","HU","US"]`: two clusters, weights **6** and **1**, dominance `12 > 7`,
  `panes[0].codes === ["AT","CZ","DE","GB","HR","HU"]`, main span **30.2827° × 16.1550°**, `viewBox`
  **`"-8.1779 -59.2407 31.494 17.3663"`** — every one of those strings and numbers unchanged, because none
  of those six codes has more than one part. **The US inset changes and it changes for the better**:
  104.83° × 52.44° → **57.72° × 24.31°** (`viewBox` `"-125.8416 -50.5435 60.0314 26.618"`), with Alaska,
  Hawaii and the Aleutians in a **41.81° × 52.44°** detached pane. The sample gains a third pane. That is a
  visible change to the shipped sample, it is stated here rather than discovered, and the pinned criterion in
  `ROADMAP.md` moves with it — I-8h re-pins all four strings.
- **A-48 C9 is untouched in mechanism.** Paint order is still descending index position over the emitted
  array. What changes is that the emitted array is now a list of **(code, pane)** pairs rather than of
  codes — see Part 4 — and Part 5 corrects the one sentence of C9 that was false.

**Part 4 — the frame shape.**

```ts
export type WorldMapPane = {
  /** 'main' | 'inset-1' | 'inset-2' | 'detached'. Positional, stable, deterministic. */
  id: string;
  /** A-49 C8″ adds the third value. */
  role: 'main' | 'inset' | 'detached';
  viewBox: string;
  bounds: core.MapBounds;
  codes: CountryCode[];
  /** Σ tripIds.length over `codes`. On the detached pane this DOUBLE-COUNTS by design — see below. */
  weight: number;
  aspect: number;
};

export type WorldMapCountry = {
  code: CountryCode;
  /** The parts of `code` drawn in THIS pane, concatenated in index order. Never the whole country. */
  d: string;
  provisional: boolean;
  tripIds: string[];
  paneId: string;
};

export type WorldMapFrame = {
  viewBox: string;          // === panes[0].viewBox
  bounds: core.MapBounds;   // === panes[0].bounds
  /** 1…4 entries; panes[0].role === 'main'; a 'detached' pane, if present, is last. */
  panes: WorldMapPane[];
  /** The PAINT list: one entry per (code, pane). A code with a detached part appears twice. */
  countries: WorldMapCountry[];
  /** A-49 Part 5: every DRAWN code exactly once, canonical row order. The chip list renders this. */
  codes: CountryCode[];
  missing: CountryCode[];
};
```

Three consequences, all stated rather than discovered:

1. **A country can be drawn in two panes, and this is the only way constraint 1 and A-41 I4 can both hold.**
   I4 requires a pane's `viewBox` to strictly contain every vertex it draws; constraint 1 forbids dropping
   any geometry; so geometry the pane will not frame must be drawn **somewhere else**, and constraint 3 says
   that somewhere is a captioned, tappable inset — not a crop and not a footnote. Both entries for a code
   carry the same `tripIds` and `provisional`, so the tap, the highlight and the attribution are identical
   in both. Within any single pane a code still appears exactly once, so W3's string-equality filter and the
   renderer's `key={c.code}` are unchanged.
2. **`pane.weight` no longer sums to `W` across panes**, because the detached pane repeats a weight already
   counted in the pane holding the same code's principal part. It is kept as `Σ tripIds.length` over the
   pane's own codes so a caption can honestly say *"US · 1 trip"*, and **nothing may re-derive `W` from
   `panes`** — C5 and C6 run over clusters, before the detached pane exists. Invariant I15.
3. **The detached pane's caption may not say *"shown separately"*.** That phrase asserts the country is a
   distant part of the traveller's record; here it is a distant part of the country's *geometry*, and the
   country is already on another pane. The caption names the codes and says so — *"distant parts of"* is
   the sense required; the exact words are the surface's. `aria-label` gains the matching third branch.

**Part 5 — R37-3: the chip list renders `frame.codes`, and A-48 C9's consequence 2 is corrected.**

A-48 C9 consequence 2 says the code-chip list *"is unchanged and complete"* and *"alphabetical"*. **Round 37
measured that as false** — C9 reordered `frame.countries`, the view renders that array verbatim
(`WorldMap.tsx`'s `.codelist`), and the rendered chips went from `AT CZ DE GB HR HU US` to
`US DE GB HU AT CZ HR`. **That sentence is withdrawn as false.** Reachability was never affected — round 37
asserted `MF` and `SX` both still present and drillable — but *complete and alphabetical* was the claim, and
only the first half was true.

**It is fixed in the contract, not in the view, and A-49 is why it has to be.** After Part 4,
`frame.countries` is a **paint list** with a duplicate row for any country that has a detached part; a view
that renders it as a country list would print `FR` twice and hand React two identical keys. Letting a UI
derive a country list from a paint list is the same class of error C9 caused in the first place. So:

> **The frame carries `codes: CountryCode[]` — every drawn code exactly once, in canonical row order — and
> `WorldMap.tsx`'s chip list renders `frame.codes` and nothing else.** The view neither sorts nor dedupes:
> `.sort(`, `new Set(` and `Object.keys(` do not appear in the file, which is a greppable ceiling of the
> same kind as W1's.

Why the chip list is worth a contract line at all, rather than a shrug: A-48 residue 6 makes it the
**named fallback** for a country no paint order can surface (`MF`/`SX`), and A-41 constraint 3's *"visibly
represented and attributable"* is discharged there. A fallback that silently changes its ordering rule
because a different array got sorted is a fallback nobody is maintaining. Restated as invariant I13.

**Part 6 — cost, measured before ruling.**

- `countryParts` over all 239 shipped codes: **26,146 intra-code ring pairs** in total (the ceiling is `MV`
  at 177 rings, 15,576 pairs) and **2.0 ms** end to end, against C3′'s 28,441 country pairs. One pass over
  the same 22,220 vertices `countryKeyPoint` already walks.
- The per-pane in-frame pass is `clusterPoints` over that pane's parts: at the 239-code ceiling **242 parts**,
  ~29,000 pairs, once per pane.
- **Only 3 of 239 codes have more than one part at 4,000 km: `UM`, `FR`, `US`** — so a detached pane exists
  only for a library containing one of them, and it holds at most a handful of parts. That is a property of
  the *shipped* index (1:110m base, 1:10m fill for 64 codes) and residue 3 records what happens if that
  changes.

**Part 7 — the four cases this rule had to survive, worked, because three rounds have now touched this area.**

| library | A-48 as shipped | A-49 | what it proves |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`FR` + `GR`** (the ship gate) | 81.13° × 49.10°, 1.95% land | **31.20° × 16.23°, 14.02% land**; French Guiana in a 2.87° × 3.70° pane at 59.8% land | the named defect is closed, and the outlier is *more* visible than it has ever been |
| **`FR` alone** | 64.08° × 49.10° | **14.15° × 9.77°** (metropolitan France + Corsica) + the identical 2.87° × 3.70° detached pane | no regression, and the honest answer to *"does a solo France still show French Guiana"* is **yes, larger than before, in a pane that names `FR`** |
| **`AT CZ DE ES FR IT`** | 73.38° × 52.93° | **28.25° × 19.04°**, same detached pane | it generalises with no per-count-of-companions branch; the rule never counts companions |
| **`US` alone / `US CA MX`** | 104.83° × 52.44° either way | **57.72° × 24.31°** alone; **119.14° × 68.69°, unchanged**, with Canada present | **this is the fourth case, and it is the important one.** Alaska is 1.5 M km², 19% of the country's area and no kind of rounding artifact — the rule detaches it from a US-only pane and **keeps it in-frame the moment Canada is in the pane**, because it is then genuinely connected to the pane's subject. Nothing about that reads *"overseas territory"*; it is connectivity, evaluated per pane |

The last row is the general answer to the hypothetical the round asked for: **a huge secondary landmass is
not treated differently from a small one, and neither is treated as a special case at all.** What decides is
whether it is chained to the pane's subject at the same threshold that decided the pane, which is exactly
the consistency whose absence was R37-1.

**Part 8 — invariants: amended, and five new.**

- **I1 (restated).** Every code in `stats.countries` appears **at least once** in `countries` **or** exactly
  once in `missing`, never both and never neither. (It was *"exactly once in `countries`"*; a code with a
  detached part now appears twice, in two different panes.)
- **I2 (restated again).** Every `country.paneId` names a pane in `panes`; every `pane.codes` is exactly the
  set of codes carrying that `paneId`, in canonical row order; **within one pane a code appears at most
  once**. The `countries` array's own order is still C9's paint order.
- **I3 (restated).** The **geographic** pane count is 1 when there is one cluster or C5's dominance test
  fails, otherwise `min(clusters, 3)`; the detached pane exists iff at least one part is detached;
  `panes.length` is that sum, and is 1…4.
- **I5 (restated).** `panes[0].role === 'main'`; a `'detached'` pane, if present, is `panes[panes.length-1]`
  and is the only one; every other pane's role is `'inset'`.
- **I11 (new) — nothing is cropped and nothing is drawn twice.** For every drawn code, the multiset of rings
  across all its `WorldMapCountry` entries is **exactly** the code's full ring set from the index, each ring
  present exactly once. This is A-41 constraint 1 made mechanical: it is the test that catches *"we made the
  frame tighter by dropping geometry"*, which is the one failure this ruling could plausibly cause.
- **I12 (new) — the key point is preserved.** For every code and every threshold,
  `countryParts(code, index, t).find(p => p.principal).key` equals `countryKeyPoint(code, index)` on both
  fields under `Object.is`. This is what makes A-48's C2′, I8 and C4′ untouched rather than merely believed
  untouched.
- **I13 (new) — the chip list is complete and canonical.** `frame.codes` contains every drawn code exactly
  once, in canonical row order, and is disjoint from `missing`.
- **I14 (new) — every pane still contains what it draws.** A-41 I4 holds **per pane over the rings actually
  drawn in that pane** — which is the reading that makes it true again; under C8 it was true only because
  the pane was too wide.
- **I15 (new) — the detached pane never decides anything.** C5's `W`, C5's comparison and C6's ordering are
  computed over clusters, before any pane exists, and no code path derives them from `panes`.
- **I4, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10 are unchanged**, and round 37 verified all of them; this ruling may not cost any
  of them. I6 (byte-identical determinism) is unthreatened: both new `clusterPoints` calls are connected
  components, which are order-independent by construction.

**Part 9 — where it lives, and the export surface.**

`countryParts` goes in **`packages/core/src/derive/country.ts`, beside `countryKeyPoint`**, for A-48 Part 2's
reason verbatim: a country's parts are a geometric property of the **index**, as `box`, `countryOf` and the
key point already are, and deriving them in `packages/client` would put a second bounds computation there —
which A-40 clause 2 forbids in as many words — and deny them to core's own tests and to I-8b. **That file's
standing guard is extended, not weakened:** the ring-area helper stays module-private, **there is still no
distance function in that file** (the linkage is `clusterPoints`', in `derive/cluster.ts`), and a part is a
*label for a country's geometry*, never an answer about a coordinate — `countryOf`'s `null` stays
first-class and nothing may snap a point to the nearest part. §2.10 moves **78 → 79** for this one symbol,
under **P2** (this section names it) and **P1** (`worldMapFrame` calls it). `CountryPart` is a type and is
not counted (§2.10's set equality is over runtime symbols).

**Part 10 — residues, stated rather than solved.**

1. **A detached part is never adopted by a neighbouring pane.** A library of `FR` and `BR` puts Brazil in one
   pane, metropolitan France in another, and French Guiana — 100 km from Brazil's own coastline — in the
   detached pane rather than in Brazil's. Adopting it would mean asking *"which pane is this part nearest
   to"*, which needs a tie-break between panes and reintroduces exactly the arbitrariness A-48 C3′ removed
   from the partition. Bounded and honest: the part is drawn, captioned by its own code, and tappable.
   **Reopen if a real library shows a detached part inside another pane's frame**, which is when the
   duplication becomes visible rather than merely inelegant.
2. **The detached pane can be wide**, for A-41 residue 3's reason one level down: it is the union of every
   detached part of every pane, and two of them can be on opposite sides of the world. On the shipped index
   the worst reachable case is a library containing `FR`, `US` and `UM` at once. It is capped at one pane
   because four insets on a phone are four illegible insets — C7's own argument, unchanged.
3. **The part count is a property of the index's scale, not of the world.** At the shipped mixed resolution
   only `UM`, `FR` and `US` have more than one part; a 1:10m index for every code would give many countries
   an island part and make the detached pane common. Nothing breaks — the rule is scale-free — but the
   *frequency* of the fourth pane is not predicted by today's measurement. **This reopens with §8.4 A-26's
   ordering/scale rule, exactly as C9 does**, and the trigger is a regeneration of `countries.gen.ts` at a
   different scale.
4. **`UM` is unfixed and this ruling does not claim otherwise.** Its in-frame part is a **344°-wide chain**
   across the Pacific — Wake to Palmyra to Johnston, each hop under 4,000 km — so its pane is globe-wide
   through A-48 residue 5's single-linkage chaining, not through C8. A-48's reopen trigger for that
   (*"a main pane wider than ~120° through a chain"*, remedy: a diameter cap on a component) is the one that
   covers it, and it is still deliberately not built.
5. **A country with a detached part is two tab stops, not one**, and appears twice in the tab order — once
   per pane, in each pane's paint order. It is one chip in the chip list (I13). Disclosed because A-48 C9
   consequence 2's mistake was exactly this class of unstated ordering consequence.
6. **A-41 Part 7's do-not-build list is unchanged except for the pane cap.** Still no manual reframe
   control, no re-clustering UI, no threshold slider, no continuous zoom or pan, no per-screen-size
   **frame** rule, no projection change, no dateline-aware bounds, no geometry simplification, and no
   *"drop the outlier"* option — the last of which this ruling is the opposite of.

#### A-50 — the pane box is the map, in both directions (revision 34, QA **R37-4**; ROADMAP **I-8h**)

**The finding.** A-48 Part 6 fixed the **wide** direction — `aspect-ratio: var(--pane-aspect)` with a static
`max-height` clamp took the reference main pane from 42.6% of its box to 100% at 390 px. It is one-sided.
At 390 px the box is 356 wide and clamped at 460 tall, so a pane fills it exactly when `aspect ≥ 356/460 =
0.774`; **50 of 239** single-country libraries do not (`MV` 0.170, `CL` 0.258, `BZ` 0.45), and `CL` measures
**33.4%** on the rendered DOM. The same clamp letterboxes the shipped sample **horizontally** on a desktop:
**87.1%** at 1100 × 900 and **76.8%** at 1440 × 700. Not a regression — it is what the fixed height did
before — but A-48 Part 6 disclosed only the wide direction, and half a fix presented as a whole one is the
class of statement this arc keeps having to correct.

**Ruling — fix it now, and the fix is one declaration, not a second mechanism.** The pane's box stops being
*"full width, clamped height, letterbox the remainder"* and becomes *"the largest box of the pane's own
aspect that fits the available width and the height cap"*:

> The height cap moves into a custom property (`--pane-cap`, `min(58vh, 460px)` for the main pane and
> `min(22vh, 170px)` for an inset — the two values already in the stylesheet), and the `<svg>` is sized
> `width: min(100%, calc(var(--pane-cap) * var(--pane-aspect)))` with `aspect-ratio: var(--pane-aspect)`,
> `max-height: var(--pane-cap)` and `margin-inline: auto`. A tall pane then gets a narrow box instead of a
> wide box with a narrow map in it; a wide pane is unchanged.

Three things this is and is not:

- **It is still measurement-free**, so W1, A-41 Part 7's *"no per-screen-size rule"* and A-48 Part 6's
  clarification of it all hold unchanged: `min()` and `calc()` over a custom property resolve at layout and
  measure nothing, no `viewBox` moves, no pane count or membership varies with screen size, and the frame is
  byte-identical in bare Node. The view still passes `pane.aspect` through and does no arithmetic
  (A-40 Part 2).
- **It does not make a narrow country bigger, and may not be described as if it does.** The Maldives in an
  equirectangular projection is a 78 px column at 390 px, and the only ways to change that are a projection
  change or `preserveAspectRatio="none"` — a distortion — both of which A-41 Part 7 forbids. What the fix
  removes is the **wasted box**, not the narrowness.
- **The criterion is symmetric, which is the part that was missing.** Not *"fills ≥ 75% of its box"* — that
  is satisfiable by luck in one direction. **No pane is letterboxed in either direction**: the painted map's
  rendered width equals the `<svg>`'s rendered width and its height equals the `<svg>`'s rendered height, to
  within 1 px, over all 239 single-country libraries **and** the reference sample, at **390 × 820 and
  1440 × 700**. Injected fault: restore the `width: 100%` + static `max-height` rule and `MV` returns to
  22.0%, `CL` to 33.4% and the sample to 76.8% at 1440 × 700.

**Residue.** A tall pane now leaves empty page beside it rather than empty box around it. `margin-inline:
auto` centres it; that is a layout consequence and it belongs in layout, which is the whole reason this is
CSS and not a frame field. Nothing else in A-48 Part 6 moves — `aspect` stays on the pane, computed in the
frame, for the reason Part 6 gives.

#### A-51 — the frame is one pane per geographic cluster: the split test, the "main" pane and the inset hierarchy are withdrawn (revision 35, QA **R38-2** MAJOR, **R38-3**, **R38-4**; ROADMAP **I-8i**)

> **STATUS: RULED, AND HELD FOR JACOB.** He asked for the framing abstraction to be reconsidered from
> first principles rather than patched a fifth time, and he asked to approve the answer **before** a
> builder pass. **No increment may be dispatched against A-51 or A-52 until he has ruled.** This entry
> is the recommendation and its evidence; it is not yet a build order. If he declines it, A-41…A-50
> stand unchanged and R38-2 stays open as a disclosed defect.

*(This ruling **supersedes A-41's C5, C6 and C7**, **A-49's C7′, C8′ and C8″**, and A-41 Part 5's/A-49
Part 4's `role` field, **in place**. Unchanged and still binding: **A-40** in full (it is not a port; W1;
W2; the projection; `missing`; no memoisation), **A-41 Part 1's diagnosis**, **Part 2's four constraints**,
**C1**, **Part 4's padding term**, **Part 6's one-kernel requirement**, **W3**, and Part 7's do-not-build
list minus the pane cap; **A-42** in full; **A-48's C2′, C3′, C4′, C9 and Part 6**; **A-49's P
(`countryParts`)**; **A-50**, which this ruling extends rather than moves. **Nothing in `packages/core`
changes except what A-52 below rules**, and `derive/cluster.ts` gets a zero-line diff for the ~~third~~
**second** increment running *(MGR-4, corrected by **A-54** Part 4: it last moved at I-8g / `53cdcc1`, so
I-8h and I-8i are the two consecutive zero-diff increments; I-8j makes it three)*. **A-54 supersedes G5's
third key and the whole of G7 — read it first.** A builder then reads **A-51** — it names which of
A-41/A-48/A-49 to skip — then
A-41 C1 + Part 4, A-48 C2′/C3′/C4′/C9 + Part 6, A-49 Part 2 (`countryParts`), A-50, then A-40 Parts 2–5.)*

**Part 1 — why this is a reopening and not a fifth patch.**

Four rounds have now ruled on one question: *which countries does the default lifetime frame show, and at
what rectangle.* A-41 built the atlas frame; A-48 fixed the key point and the partition; A-49 fixed the
extent. Each fixed exactly what the previous round measured, each was implemented faithfully — round 36, 37
and 38 all confirmed *"the defect is in what the ruling specifies, not in what was built"* — and each was
followed by the same class of finding one clause further out. Round 38 is where the pattern becomes
diagnosable rather than merely annoying:

> **R38-2 (MAJOR).** A-49 closed every case where **C5 decides to split**. On the cases where C5 declines —
> **22,765 of 28,441 (80.0%)** two-country / one-trip-each libraries hold two clusters in one un-split pane —
> the original defect is **untouched**. `FR`+`US` renders **one 134.2° × 26.1° pane laid out 356 × 80 px**,
> in which **France paints 36 × 25 px = 899 px²** (round 37 filed MAJOR on Greece at **783 px²**);
> `FR`+`NZ` is 183.1° × 97.8° at **0.48% land** (R37-1 was 2.22%); `GB`+`AU` 161.1° × 102.3° at 4.02%;
> `US`+`JP` 270.2° × 24.3° at 8.91%. A-49 *improved* every one of them and fixed none.

Round 38 also proved, independently, that **A-49's own premise is false in general**: the builder's KD-72 and
the breaker both measured the `US`+`JP` pane's in-frame set at **2** components, so A-49 Part 2's *"the
in-frame set is exactly one component"* holds only for a pane that **is** one cluster. The shipped code
implements the written union rule correctly and no behaviour follows — but the proof A-49 rests on is a
proof about one-cluster panes, and C5/C7 hand it panes that are not.

**That is the shape of the defect, and it is structural.** The model decides, **once**, whether to split,
and then draws exactly one thing called *the main pane*. Both halves are wrong:

1. **The split test asks the wrong question of the wrong quantity.** C5 splits iff `2 × weight(primary) > W`
   — a question about how much of the traveller's *record* one cluster carries. Legibility is a question
   about **geometry**: two clusters 6,900 km apart do not fit one rectangle legibly whether the record is
   split 13–1 or 1–1. C5 correctly refuses to break a tie by alphabet (that refusal is right and survives),
   but a tie is exactly what a two-country traveller with one trip each has, so the rule's *stated*
   abstention is also its **majority** case. A rule whose failure mode is concentrated on its ties should
   stop having ties in it.
2. **The no-split branch's fallback is the worst frame available.** When no cluster dominates, C7 puts
   *every* cluster in one rectangle. So the answer to *"this history has no single subject"* is *"then draw
   all of it at once"* — which is the 194.5° frame R33-1 opened this whole arc to remove. A model whose
   default branch is the original defect cannot be finished by adding conditions to the other branch.
3. **"Main" is a claim the geometry cannot support.** C7's third pane is the *union of clusters 3…N*, framed
   as one rectangle — a multi-component box by construction, which is the same defect at pane index 2.
   A-49 then had to add a **fourth** pane for the geometry the first three would not frame. Four pane kinds,
   three of which can be multi-component, is not a model; it is an accumulation.

**A country's rendered size currently depends on where the traveller's *other* countries are.** That is the
sentence. Rounds 36, 37 and 38 each measured **one library at a time**, and this property is only visible by
comparing two libraries — which is why it survived three adversarial rounds that broke everything else.

**Part 2 — the invariant, stated so it can be tested.**

What *"looked at by a human and judged legible"* actually required in rounds 36–38 was three things: the
pane is not mostly ocean, the smallest attributed territory is big enough to see and press, and the pane is
not wide because of something that is not its subject. Stated as invariants of the default frame:

> **L1 — tightness (structural).** Every pane's `bounds` is the bounding box of **exactly one connected
> component** of country *parts* at `WORLD_CLUSTER_THRESHOLD_KM`. Equivalently: the parts a pane frames
> admit a spanning tree every edge of which is shorter than the threshold. **No pane contains a jump wider
> than the threshold.** Corollary, and it is a theorem rather than a measurement: a pane's diameter is at
> most `Σᵢ diam(partᵢ) + (n−1) × threshold`. A pane can be wide **only** because its own countries are big
> or because a genuine chain of visited ground spans it — never because two things it shows are far apart.
>
> **L2 — locality (relational).** For any library `A` and any code `x ∉ A`: in `A ∪ {x}`, every pane of `A`
> whose component gains no part of `x` appears with a **byte-identical** `viewBox`, `bounds` and `codes`.
> A country's rendered size is a function of **its own cluster** and of the cell it is drawn in, and of
> nothing else in the library. **This is the invariant main+inset cannot have, and R38-2 is a violation of
> it**: `FR` alone frames 14.15° × 9.77°; `FR`+`US` frames France at 134.2° × 26.1°.
>
> **L3 — subject legibility (measured, on the reference viewport).** Every drawn code has exactly one
> **home** pane — the pane holding its principal part — and at **390 × 820 css px** its rendered bounding
> box there is **≥ 24 × 24 px** (WCAG 2.5.8's target size; 576 px², against the 783 px² and 899 px² that
> rounds 37 and 38 filed as MAJOR). **L3 is not universally satisfiable and this ruling does not claim it
> is**: a micro-state inside a large cluster is sub-pixel at any frame that also shows its neighbours
> (`VA` 0 × 0, `MC` 1 × 1 in a France–Germany–Italy pane), and the only remedies are per-country insets or a
> distorting projection, both of which A-41 Part 7 forbids. Part 5 measures it; Part 8 residue 1 states the
> exception and names the guarantee that covers it.
>
> > **Amended by A-54 Part 4 (QA R39-7): the exception is widened to name residue 3 as well.** L3 also
> > fails for a code whose *own* planar box straddles ±180 — measured, a single-country `FJ` library renders
> > an `<svg>` of **356 × 16 css px** with Fiji at **342.2 × 2.2 = 753 px²** at 390 × 820, in a library with
> > no cluster and no micro-state, i.e. outside the exception as first written. That is **residue 3**, not
> > residue 1, and residue 3 owns it; A-48 residue 6's chip list is the guarantee that covers both cases.
> > **The exception reads: a micro-state inside a large cluster (residue 1), *or* a code whose own box
> > straddles the antimeridian (residue 3) — and nothing wider.**
>
> **L4 — completeness (non-negotiable, unchanged).** Every drawn code is in at least one pane; the multiset
> of rings across a code's entries is exactly the index's ring set for that code, each ring once; nothing is
> dropped, cropped, hidden or re-scaled. A-41 constraint 1, verbatim.
>
> **L5 — geometry-derived (non-negotiable, unchanged).** Nothing reads which country a code is, what
> continent it is on, or what kind of destination it is. Proof obligation: permuting every ISO code in the
> index leaves every pane byte-identical — the test round 38 already built and ran.

L1 and L2 are the two the current model cannot state, let alone hold. L1 fails on every un-split pane; L2
fails on 80% of two-country libraries.

**Part 3 — the models weighed, and the one chosen.**

- **Keep main+inset, replace C5's trigger with a legibility one** (land fraction, or a minimum rendered
  size). **Rejected, and this is round 39's version of the same patch.** Three reasons, in order of weight.
  (a) It still decides *"is this bad enough?"* rather than *"is this tight?"*, so the wide side of whatever
  threshold it uses is illegible **by construction** — the rule guarantees a worst case equal to its own
  bound. (b) A land fraction is not computable without rasterising the pane, i.e. a point-in-polygon engine
  in `packages/client` — the second geometry implementation A-40 Part 5, A-48 Part 2 and A-49 Part 9 have
  each refused. (c) It keeps the hierarchy, so a genuine tie still has to demote a cluster or refuse to
  split, and the tie is the majority case. Every previous round's fix was *"add a condition"*; this is the
  fourth one.
- **A single frame with a broken axis / adaptive projection.** **Rejected on honesty.** A-41 Part 7 and A-50
  already forbid `preserveAspectRatio="none"` and any projection change, because a map that lies about shape
  and distance is a legibility failure of its own kind, and there is no visible chrome to disclose the break
  (the *"no placeholder UI, presentation stays honest"* constraint from the original visual direction).
  It also does not actually work: `FR`+`NZ` needs the break to swallow ~19,000 km of Pacific, at which point
  the two survivors are two tight frames with a seam drawn between them — i.e. it is small multiples with a
  distortion added and a boundary hidden. The honest limit of the idea *is* the recommended model.
- **Always split, keep the three-pane cap.** **Rejected**: C7's *"union of every remaining cluster"* pane is
  a multi-component rectangle by definition, so it violates L1 at pane index 2, and A-49's detached pane
  then has to exist to catch what it will not frame. This is the recommended model with a cap and a
  hierarchy bolted on, and both bolts are where the defects live.
- **Insets drawn inside the main map, true atlas-style.** **Rejected**: placement needs either arithmetic in
  the view (W1/W2) or a layout engine in `packages/client`. Measurement-freedom is the property the whole
  design rests on (A-40 Part 4).
- **★ One pane per geographic cluster. No "main", no inset, no split test.** **Recommended.** The frame is a
  set of equally-weighted rectangles, one per connected component of parts, laid out in a grid and ordered
  by how much of the record each carries. It satisfies L1 by definition, L2 by construction, and L4/L5
  unchanged. It is **smaller** than what it replaces: one partition instead of three (C3′'s country pass,
  C8′'s per-pane pass, C8″'s union), one pane kind instead of four, no dominance test, no cap, no
  tie-break-by-alphabet, and one fewer call into the kernel.

The cost, stated before the benefits: **Jacob's stated mechanism — *"preserving meaningful outliers visibly
through an inset"* — is overturned.** His *purpose* clause is not: *"rather than allowing a single distant
point to compress the primary trip/history geography into an unreadable frame"* is satisfied maximally,
because under this model **no cluster can compress any other cluster at all**, which is exactly L2. And
*"prioritize the main geographic cluster"* survives as **reading order**: `panes[0]` is still the cluster
carrying most of the record, still first, still full width, still at the top. What it loses is the claim
that the other clusters are *lesser frames*. That claim is what produced 899 px² France.

**Part 4 — the contract. `worldMapFrame` implements exactly this and nothing more.**

- **G1 — the population.** A-41 **C1**, unchanged: every row of `stats.countries` in canonical order
  (ascending ISO code), minus the codes the index cannot fill, which go to `missing` and are stated in
  words (A-40 clause 3).
- **G2 — the atoms are parts, and the canonical part list is the frame's only ordinal.** For each drawn code,
  `core.countryParts(code, index, WORLD_CLUSTER_THRESHOLD_KM)` — A-49 Part 2's `P`, unchanged, plus A-52's
  correction. A code with **no** parts goes to `missing`. The **canonical part list** is: drawn codes in
  canonical row order, each code's parts in `countryParts`' own order. Every ordering decision below is a
  position in this list, so no `Map`/`Set` iteration order and no second sort key is ever needed.
- **G3 — one partition, and every component is a pane.** `core.clusterPoints(list.map(p => p.key),
  WORLD_CLUSTER_THRESHOLD_KM)` — **one call**, A-48 C3′'s connected-components semantics, A-41 Part 6's one
  kernel. **Each component is a pane. There are no other panes and there is no other partition.** This
  clause is what supersedes **C3′'s country-level call** (subsumed: two countries share a pane iff two of
  their parts are within the threshold, which is C3′ exactly when every code has one part, and is the
  *correct* generalisation when it does not), **C5** (deleted — there is no split decision left to make),
  **C7/C7′** (deleted — there is no cap and no union-of-the-rest pane), **C8′** (subsumed — a pane is one
  component, so *"frame the parts your subject is connected to"* is now the definition rather than a repair)
  and **C8″** (deleted — a detached part is simply a component, therefore a pane, therefore already drawn,
  captioned and tappable).
- **G4 — what a pane is.**

  ```ts
  export type WorldMapPane = {
    /** `p0`…`pN`. Positional, stable, deterministic. */
    id: string;
    /** Every code with a part in this component, canonical row order. The caption is written from these. */
    codes: CountryCode[];
    /** The codes whose PRINCIPAL part is here. Every drawn code is `home` in exactly one pane. */
    home: CountryCode[];
    /** Σ tripIds.length over `home`. Additive: Σ over panes === W, exactly. */
    weight: number;
    /** Core's own `MapBounds` over the four corners of each member part's `box`. UNpadded. */
    bounds: core.MapBounds;
    /** "minX minY width height", padded per A-41 Part 4. The ONLY fit mechanism. */
    viewBox: string;
    /** width / height of the padded viewBox — A-48 Part 6, unchanged. */
    aspect: number;
  };
  ```

  `role` is **withdrawn**. There is one kind of pane. `bounds` is one `core.mapBounds` call per pane over
  the member parts' box corners — the client still computes no bounds, and A-49 C8′'s mechanism sentence
  survives verbatim. `viewBox` and `aspect` are A-41 Part 4 and A-48 Part 6 unchanged.

  **`weight` becomes additive again**, which A-49 Part 4 consequence 2 had to give up. Every code has
  exactly one principal part (A-48 C2′), hence exactly one home pane, so `Σ pane.weight === W` for every
  library. A pane holding only non-principal parts has `home === []` and `weight === 0`.
- **G5 — the order, total and deterministic.** `weight` descending, then `home.length` descending, then the
  component's **lowest position in the canonical part list** ascending. The third key is total by
  construction — positions are unique — so unlike C6 there is no tie left for the alphabet to break, and no
  library can produce two panes the ordering cannot separate. `panes[0]` is the cluster carrying most of the
  record. **That is the whole of what weight decides now**: it orders, it does not frame.

  > **Superseded in part by A-54 Part 3 (QA R39-5). The third key is replaced; keys 1 and 2 stand.** The
  > canonical part list is built from ISO-sorted codes, so *"there is no tie left for the alphabet to break"*
  > is **false** — it was the alphabet, one indirection out, in **99.5%** of two-country libraries with two
  > or more panes. **G5′ is: `weight` desc, `home.length` desc, `bounds.north` **desc**, `bounds.west`
  > **asc**, then the canonical position.** The pane's own rectangle decides, latitude first because it has
  > no ±180 seam; the canonical position survives **as the last key, named as the alphabet**, and is measured
  > as deciding **0** adjacent pairs over 30,680 libraries. **I18 is untouched** — it is a theorem of key 1.
- **G6 — no cap, and no pane is a union of clusters.** `panes.length` is the number of components. Measured
  on the shipped index (Part 5): **1** for a 239-code library, **1–4** for a two-country library, **8** for a
  twelve-country worldwide library, and ~~**14**~~ **18** for the greedy worst case (a library chosen so
  that no two parts are within the threshold — **corrected by A-54 Part 4, QA R39-3**: 60,000 randomised
  greedy passes find `AQ AU CL EH FJ GL GU IO MS MX PK PN RO RU RW SH TF VN`, 18 codes → **18 panes, all 18
  of them home panes**). A cap is refused because a cap is exactly C7 — the union pane it needs is
  a multi-component rectangle and reintroduces the defect. Many panes is the *correct* degradation: each one
  is still tight on its own subject, whereas the alternative degrades to a single rectangle in which
  everything is a speck.
- **G7 — the panes are laid out as an equal grid, and this is layout, not frame.**
  > **SUPERSEDED IN FULL BY A-54 Part 1 (manager's I-8i gate, MGR-1). Read G7′ there, not this clause.**
  > The grid's rows are as tall as their tallest cell and its last row has as many cells as it has items, so
  > `align-items: start` left up to **66.7%** of the card painting in the separator ink (one-pane libraries
  > at ≥ 960 px; 45.6% on `FR`+`US`, 29.0% on the Europe 2026 fixture), and `minmax(300px, 1fr)` **overflowed
  > and clipped** at a 320 px viewport. G7′ is a wrapping flex line box whose cells fill their line, which
  > makes `Σ cell area = container area − gaps` structurally. **R38-3 is still fixed** — by G7″ (no cell
  > draws a boundary of its own) rather than by this clause's cell criterion, which A-54 withdraws.
  >
  > *What follows is kept for the record and is not the shipped rule.*

  `.worldmap__panes`
  becomes `display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(var(--pane-min, 300px), 1fr));
  align-items: start;` — one column at 390 px, three at 1440 px for the reference sample. Every cell carries
  **one** height cap, `--pane-cap: min(38vh, 300px)`; the role-dependent two-value cap
  (`min(58vh,460px)` / `min(22vh,170px)`) is withdrawn with `role`. The `<svg>` rule is **A-50's, verbatim
  and unchanged**. This is measurement-free for A-48 Part 6's reason, which A-50 restates and this clause
  does not weaken: `min()`, `calc()`, `auto-fill` and a media query resolve at layout and measure nothing;
  no `viewBox`, pane count or pane membership varies with screen size; the frame is byte-identical in bare
  Node.

  **R38-3 is fixed here rather than separately.** A-50's criterion measured the `<svg>` and not the bordered
  **cell**, and a flex row stretches every cell to its tallest sibling (the sample's US inset fell to
  **44.1%** of its cell, a four-pane `inset-2` to **21.3%**). `align-items: start` on a grid does not
  stretch, and one uniform cap removes the asymmetry that made the stretch large. **The criterion becomes
  the cell:** `cell.height − svg.height − caption.height − padding ≤ 1 px`, at 390 × 820 and 1440 × 700,
  over the library set A-50 already uses.

  **R38-4 is fixed structurally, not by a rule.** French Guiana was **7 × 8 px = 56 px²** because C8″ put it
  in one rectangle with Alaska and Hawaii, 120.1° × 69.3° wide. Under G3 it is its own component, therefore
  its own pane: **223 × 288 px** on `FR`+`US` and **223 × 288 px** on `FR` alone (Part 5). A-49 residues 1
  and 2 go with it — a detached part **is** adopted by a neighbouring cluster when it is genuinely connected
  to one (French Guiana joins a Peru pane, Part 5 case D), which is what residue 1 named as its own reopen
  trigger, and there is no union-of-detached pane left to be wide.
- **G8 — the caption, derived rather than roled.** Every pane names its `codes` (A-41 constraint 3, now
  applied uniformly — under C7 the main pane had no caption because it was *"the"* map, and there is no
  *"the"* map any more). A pane with `home.length === 0` is captioned ***"distant parts of"*** and may not
  say *"shown separately"* — **A-49 Part 4 consequence 3's rule survives verbatim**, now derived from
  `home` rather than from a `role` string. `aria-label` follows the same two branches. This is a `.length`
  check in the view, not arithmetic over coordinates: A-40 Part 2 is intact and **W3 is unchanged** — the
  renderer still selects a pane's countries by `country.paneId === pane.id` and by nothing else.

**Part 5 — measured, against the geometries three rounds have used.** Every number below is my own, from
`core.countryParts` / `core.clusterPoints` / `core.mapBounds` on the shipped index, with land measured by
even-odd sampling of the pane's own rectangle at 240 × 240 and pixels computed at **390 × 820** (356 px of
content, one grid column, `--pane-cap` resolving to **300 px**, A-50's box rule). The "shipped" column is
round 38's re-derived numbers where it published them and my own re-derivation where it did not. **The two
desktop rows hold the cap at 300 px and vary only the column count** — at 1440 × 700 the real
`min(38vh, 300px)` resolves to 266 px, so the quoted desktop page heights are ~10% conservative and the
quoted widths, which are column-limited rather than cap-limited, are exact.

| **`FR` + `NZ`** — R38-2's worst land | **1 pane 183.1° × 97.8°, 0.48% land** | **3 panes**, worst land **18.98%** (**40×**); FR 43.2%, NZ 19.0%, Guiana 59.8%. Every home ≥ 284 × 236 px |
| **`GB` + `AU`** | 1 pane 161.1° × 102.3°, **4.02% land**, GB 20 × 18 = 360 px² | **2 panes**: AU 40.23°×32.97° (**48.1%**), GB 9.25°×8.67° (**39.3%**), **GB 307 × 288 = 88,416 px²** |
| **`US` + `JP`** | 1 pane 270.2° × 24.3° at 356 × 44 px, 8.9% land, JP 20 × 18 px | **3 panes**: JP 16.13°×14.52° (16.3%, **319 × 287 px**), US (52.6%), Alaska (11.8%) |
| **one outlier vs a cluster** `AT CZ DE ES FR IT JP` | 3 panes; main 28.25°×19.04° (37.1%), JP inset at **188 × 170 px** | **3 panes, main `viewBox` byte-identical**; JP gets **332 × 300 px** instead of a 188 × 170 inset. Smallest home **CZ 80 × 31 px** |
| **three real clusters** `FR DE IT JP PE` | **4 panes**: main 23.07°×18.36°, JP inset 188×170, PE inset **120 × 170 px**, detached Guiana 133×170 | **3 panes**: Europe 23.07°×18.36° (31.6%, byte-identical) · **PE 29.75°×24.10° (14.7%), and French Guiana is in it** — 2,700 km from Peru, genuinely connected, so residue 1's reopen trigger is answered rather than deferred; PE 147 × 210 px · JP 332 × 300 px. **One fewer pane than the model it replaces** |
| **compact regional only** `AT CZ DE HR HU SI` | 1 pane 16.72° × 12.50°, 37.6% land | **1 pane, byte-identical.** The model does not split a history that is genuinely one cluster |
| **worldwide, 12 codes** `US×2 BR GB FR ZA EG IN JP AU NZ TH PE` | 3 geographic panes + detached; `inset-2` is the union of clusters 3…N | **8 panes**, land 10.7 / 27.8 / 41.1 / 26.4 / 52.6 / 16.3 / 49.2 / 11.8%; smallest **home** rendering **NZ 63 × 64 px**. Page ≈ 2,393 px at 390 px, **582 px at 1440 px (4 columns)** |
| **the 239-country ceiling** | 1 pane, 360° × 173.6° | **1 pane, byte-identical, 30.3% land.** The world is one component at 4,000 km, so *"I have been everywhere"* correctly gets one honest world map |

Three census results over the whole index, which is where the claim stops being anecdote:

- **Two-country libraries, all 28,441 pairs.** Shipped: **one** geographic pane in **100%** of them (C5 never
  splits a tie, and every one-trip-each pair is a tie — round 38 measured 22,765 of these as holding two or
  more clusters). Proposed: **1 pane in 5,564** (19.6% — genuinely nearby pairs), **2 in 22,360**, **3 in
  516**, **4 in 1**. Panes wider than 120°: **8,364 pairs → 1,229**, an **85.3% reduction**.
- **Every remaining >120° pane traces to five codes.**
  > **Corrected by A-54 Part 4 (QA R39-4): this sentence counts panes and libraries in the same breath and
  > is false as written.** Re-derived over all 28,441 pairs: **1,236 panes** exceed 120° unpadded (1,237
  > padded), of which **1,187 contain one of the five** and **49 do not**; **1,229** is the count of
  > *libraries* holding at least one such pane. Of the 49: **48 span more than 180°** (the planar-bbox
  > artefact of a trans-antimeridian pair, e.g. `AS`+`MH` at 343.1°) and **exactly one is an honest wide
  > frame — `CA`+`GL` at 128.8°**, two large neighbouring countries, which is not a defect.

  `AQ`, `FJ`, `KI`, `RU`, `UM` each appear in 238 of the
  1,229, i.e. **every pair containing one of them**; the rest are Pacific micro-states chaining into `KI`/
  `UM`. That is **A-48 residue 1′ and A-49 residue 4 exactly, unchanged, and out of scope** — it needs
  dateline-aware bounds in core, which A-41 Part 1 refuses on measurement. This ruling neither fixes nor
  worsens it.
- **Pane count.** 236 of 239 single-country libraries → 1 pane; `FR`, `UM`, `US` → 2. Over 400 pseudo-random
  libraries of 1–25 codes: median **4**, maximum **8**. Greedy worst case over the whole index: ~~**14**~~
  **18** *(A-54 Part 4, QA R39-3)*.

**Part 6 — what survives, honestly and by name.** Jacob asked for a real accounting.

| thing | verdict |
|---|---|
| **`core.countryKeyPoint`** (A-48 C2′) | **Survives in core, unchanged, and loses its production caller.** G3 clusters parts, and the principal part's `key` **is** the country key point bit-for-bit (I12, 0 mismatches over 239 codes × 8 thresholds), so C2′'s *content* survives as a property of `countryParts`. It stays exported at **§2.10's 79** under **P2** — this section names it as the definition of *"where is this country"* and as **I12's oracle**, and deleting it would delete A-48's own regression guard. Disclosed: after I-8i it is the **one** symbol on the surface justified by P2 alone. That is a trim decision for whoever next audits §2.10, not for this ruling |

The frame calls the kernel **once** where it called it `1 + panes.length` times — strictly fewer calls, same semantics, same signature |

| **A-41 C4/C4′** (`WORLD_CLUSTER_THRESHOLD_KM = 4000`) | **Survives unchanged, and gets its job back.** A-49 gave it two jobs that had to agree; it now has one, and the *"no natural gap in the distribution / it is a presentation choice"* disclosure (A-48 Part 4) is unchanged and still the honest statement |

Still no manual reframe control, no re-clustering UI, no threshold slider, no continuous zoom or pan, no per-screen-size **frame** rule, no projection change, no dateline-aware bounds, no geometry simplification, and no *"drop the outlier"* option |
